epic.title: EPIC-27: Question Detail Status Labels
epic.functionalNeed:
When a user opens a question in the questions analysis and inspects how a single AI engine answered it, the status shown for that engine must read as the true outcome for the brand. Two cases currently mislabel that outcome.
In a visibility question, an engine can place the brand somewhere in its ranking or leave the brand out of the ranking entirely. The per-engine status must read with the right severity across three tiers: a strong ranking is a leading result, a weak ranking is unfavorable, and not being ranked at all is the worst possible outcome and must read as such, rather than as a neutral, muted style.
In a competitive question, each engine makes a binary head-to-head choice: it either selects the brand or it selects a competitor. A single engine's outcome is therefore always either a win or a loss. Today, when the viewed engine did not select the brand, the detail can read "Split" rather than "Lost". "Split" only describes the aggregate across several engines that disagree with each other; it is never a valid description of one engine's answer. When the engine in view did not select the brand, that engine's result must read "Lost".
This EPIC corrects both labels in the per-engine question detail so the status always reflects the real outcome. The aggregate favorability rollup across engines is unchanged: a genuine disagreement across engines still reads as "Split".
> ⚡ PM revirement — Quentin, 2026-06-22 (supersedes the previous binary model). Visibility per-engine status follows a 3-tier model: rank 1–3 → Favorable (green) with the rank shown · rank 4–10 → "Unfavorable" (yellow/amber, same color as the competitive Split banner) with the rank shown · not ranked → "Unranked" (red). Applies to BOTH the engine pill badge and the favorability card. The aggregate rollup across engines is unchanged.
---
scope: - The aggregate "Split" label and the favorability rollup logic across multiple engines
- Perception question status, which is expressed as sentiment rather than win, loss, or rank
- Any change to how rankings, win rate, or sentiment are computed
- The competitive model itself: it stays Won (green) / Lost (red), with no per-engine "Split"
- The not-ranked visibility result carries an explicit "Unranked" caption (red), distinct from the amber "Unfavorable" tier — styling alone is not used. (PM decision, 2026-06-22.)

stories.title: 27-3 — Aggregate "Split" across engines is preserved
stories.userStory:
## Story

As a viewer scanning the questions list, I want a question to still read as **"Split"** when engines genuinely disagree, so that the aggregate view keeps distinguishing mixed results from clear wins or losses.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1** — Given a question where some engines are favorable and others are not, When the aggregate status is shown across all selected engines, Then it still reads "Split".

**AC2** — Given the favorability rollup at the top of the questions analysis, When statuses are tallied, Then the counts of favorable, split, and unfavorable results are unchanged by this EPIC.

📋 Spec complète : [27-3-aggregate-split-preserved.md](https://github.com/AirPR/geo-analytics/blob/main/docs/implementation-artifacts/epics/epic-27/27-3-aggregate-split-preserved.md)

stories.title: 27-2 — Not-selected competitive result reads as "Lost"
stories.userStory:
## Story

As a viewer inspecting a competitive question, I want an engine that did **not select my brand** to read as **"Lost"**, so that I am not shown an ambiguous **"Split"** for a single engine's binary choice.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1** — Given a competitive question detail, When the viewed engine did not select the brand, Then that engine's result reads "Lost", never "Split".

**AC2** — Given a competitive question detail, When the viewed engine selected the brand, Then that engine's result reads "Won".

**AC3** — Given a competitive question, When a single engine's outcome is shown, Then "Split" never appears for that single engine because its choice is always either a win or a loss.

📋 Spec complète : [27-2-not-selected-competitive-lost.md](https://github.com/AirPR/geo-analytics/blob/main/docs/implementation-artifacts/epics/epic-27/27-2-not-selected-competitive-lost.md)

stories.title: 27-1 — Visibility per-engine status: 3-tier model (Favorable / Unfavorable / Unranked)
stories.userStory:
## Story

As a viewer inspecting a visibility question, I want each engine's outcome for my brand to read with the right severity — **Favorable** when ranked in the top 3, **Unfavorable** (amber) when ranked 4 to 10, and **Unranked** (red) when the brand is not ranked at all — so that I instantly distinguish a leading result from a weak one and from a complete miss.
stories.acceptanceCriteria:
**AC1** — Given a visibility question detail, When the viewed engine ranked the brand between rank 1 and 3 inclusive, Then the result is shown as "Favorable" in green, with the rank displayed (#1, #2 or #3).

**AC2** — Given a visibility question detail, When the viewed engine ranked the brand between rank 4 and 10 inclusive, Then the result is shown as "Unfavorable" in yellow/amber (the same shade as the competitive "Split" banner), with the rank displayed.

**AC3** — Given a visibility question detail, When the viewed engine did not rank the brand (not ranked), Then the result is shown as "Unranked" in red — a label distinct from "Unfavorable".

**AC4** — Given a single engine's visibility result, When it is shown, Then these three states (Favorable green 1–3 / Unfavorable amber 4–10 / Unranked red not-ranked) are the only possible ones, and the green/amber/red color is consistent between the engine pill badge and the favorability card.

📋 Spec complète : [27-1-not-ranked-visibility-unfavorable.md](https://github.com/AirPR/geo-analytics/blob/main/docs/implementation-artifacts/epics/epic-27/27-1-not-ranked-visibility-unfavorable.md)
